date.day().t: The timestamp to read, in milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC, such as `time`.
date.day().zone: The IANA timezone to read the timestamp in, such as `"Asia/Kolkata"`. Left out, the chart's timezone is used.

date.dayOfWeek().t: The timestamp to read, in milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC, such as `time`.
date.dayOfWeek().zone: The IANA timezone to read the timestamp in, such as `"Asia/Kolkata"`. Left out, the chart's timezone is used.

date.dayOfYear().t: The timestamp to read, in milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC, such as `time`.
date.dayOfYear().zone: The IANA timezone to read the timestamp in, such as `"Asia/Kolkata"`. Left out, the chart's timezone is used.

date.format().t: The timestamp to write, such as `time`.
date.format().pattern: The layout of the text, built from the placeholders `yyyy`, `MM`, `dd`, `HH`, `mm`, `ss`, `MMM` and `EEE`, as in `"dd MMM yyyy"`. Every other character is copied as written.
date.format().zone: The IANA timezone to write the timestamp in, such as `"Asia/Kolkata"`. Left out, the chart's timezone is used.

date.from().year: The calendar year, such as `2025`. Every field must be a whole number, or the result is `none`.
date.from().month: The month, 1 for January through 12 for December. A value outside that range rolls over, so 13 is January of the next year.
date.from().day: The day of the month, 1 to 31. A value outside the month rolls over, so day 0 is the last day of the month before.
date.from().hour: The hour on a 24 hour clock, 0 to 23.
date.from().minute: The minute of the hour, 0 to 59.
date.from().second: The second of the minute, 0 to 59.
date.from().zone: The IANA timezone the fields are read in as a wall clock time, such as `"Asia/Kolkata"`. Left out, the chart's timezone is used.

date.hour().t: The timestamp to read, in milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC, such as `time`.
date.hour().zone: The IANA timezone to read the timestamp in, such as `"Asia/Kolkata"`. Left out, the chart's timezone is used.

date.isSameDay().a: The first timestamp to compare, such as `time`.
date.isSameDay().b: The second timestamp to compare, such as `time[1]`. When either timestamp is absent, the answer is `none`.
date.isSameDay().zone: The IANA timezone whose calendar decides the day, such as `"Asia/Kolkata"`. Left out, the chart's timezone is used.
